findings.red: The final native-provider capability check disposed its owner then returned true; the baseline still invoked the in-memory send stub once. Initial callback disposal also began one validator call.
findings.green: The post-callback owned disposed check vetoes both cases: zero send calls, and zero initial validator/provider work. Existing broadcast-unknown marker survives final-check disposal.

findings.title: External signal setup/removal could reject outside Result after physical work had started
findings.red: Malformed or overridden signal accessors/listeners rejected the public Promise or admitted work; suspended validator/provider scenarios returned rejections instead of fixed results.
findings.green: Native signal brand access and captured EventTarget primitives avoid ordinary overridden hooks; unsupported signals return fixed INVALID_INPUT before work. Owned signal adaptation isolates journal calls, cleanup cannot replace Result, and active admission persists until actual physical work drains.
